facts.text: Carrollton’s real‑estate boom in the 1850s was sparked by the Jefferson and Lake Pontchartrain Railroad, which linked the town to New Orleans and the lake.
The 1855 Greek Revival Carrollton Parish Courthouse still stands, a rare surviving example of mid‑19th‑century civic architecture in the area.
The riverfront section of Carrollton, known as the Black Pearl, produced gospel legend Mahalia Jackson, the “Queen of Gospel music.”.
In 1988 the Carrollton Historic District was added to the National Register of Historic Places, preserving its unique 19th‑century streetscape.
The Nix Branch Library, operated by the New Orleans Public Library, has been a community hub since its opening and was praised by local journalist Robert Morris as a “popular little” library.
Carrollton was incorporated in 1845, then annexed by New Orleans in 1874, becoming the city’s 16th and 17th wards while keeping a distinct neighborhood feel.
